title: Moving quantum sensors
summary: We investigate whether controlled motion of a quantum sensor offers a metrological advantage in a field-detection task. We consider a localized field of known strength $B$ occupying an unknown contiguous region making up a fraction $1/N$ of the total search space, with a qubit sensor controlled for a total time $T$ to maximize the probability of detecting the field. We study the regime in which the characteristic timescale of the field is slow compared to the time to move the sensor between any two regions, and we distinguish classical motion, where the sensor follows a definite trajectory,…
